questions.prompt: A request fails with 400 Bad Request. Should the client retry it unchanged?
options: Yes: errors are usually transient
Yes, after a short wait
Only if the request was a GET
No: a 4xx means the client did something wrong

questions.prompt: Which of these HTTP methods is idempotent but not safe?
options: GET
DELETE
POST
PATCH

questions.prompt: A client sends DELETE /books/8, times out, and retries. The retry answers 404 Not Found. Was the DELETE idempotent?
options: Yes: the effect, book 8 being gone, is the same as deleting once
No: the two calls got different responses
No: the 404 means the first call never ran
Only if the server cached the first response

questions.prompt: A POST that creates an order times out, so the client doesn't know whether the order was created. How can it retry safely?
options: Send the retry as a PUT instead
GET the order list first, and retry if the order is missing
Resend it with the same idempotency key, so the server replays its earlier response instead of creating a second order
Wait a few seconds, so the first request has time to finish

questions.prompt: Why does cursor pagination (?after=137) work better than offset pagination (?offset=40) for a feed where new items keep arriving?
options: Cursors are shorter to send
The server jumps to the cursor with an index seek, and items added elsewhere don't shift the page
Offset pages can't be cached
Cursors return every item in one response

questions.prompt: A mobile app needs a book, its author, and the author's other books. Through a REST API it makes three requests, and each response carries every field. What are these two problems called?
options: Under-fetching and over-fetching
The N+1 problem and batching
Head-of-line blocking and congestion
Normalization and denormalization

questions.prompt: Why are Protocol Buffers messages much smaller than the equivalent JSON?
options: They're always gzip-compressed
They leave out fields the client didn't ask for
They're sent over UDP instead of TCP
They use a binary encoding that identifies fields by number instead of by name

questions.prompt: What's the danger in treating a remote procedure call as if it were a local function call?
options: Generated client code is slow to compile
A remote call can time out without telling you whether it ran, and it's far slower and more variable
RPC frameworks can't return errors
RPC calls can't carry structured arguments

questions.prompt: A GraphQL query asks for 50 books with each author's name. A naive resolver loads each book's author separately. How many database queries is that, and what's the fix?
options: 2, and no fix is needed
50, fixed by adding an index on authors
51, fixed by batching all the author ids into one query
1, because GraphQL loads everything at once

questions.prompt: Why doesn't ordinary HTTP caching work well for GraphQL?
options: Every query is a POST to the same URL
GraphQL responses are binary
The schema changes too often to cache
GraphQL servers forbid caching headers
